question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in continuation subsystem with trusted cross-session delegate-return delivery in this PR, or require a narrower split before merge?
rationale: The code creates a new first-party path for model-produced delegate output to enter another session as trusted internal context; automation can verify mechanics, but only maintainers can approve that trust boundary and product shape.

options.title: Require exact-head proof and boundary approval
options.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, prove the actual merge result including accepted high-context `request_compaction`, and approve the trusted return-delivery model before merge.

options.title: Split the continuation substrate
options.body: Ask for smaller PRs that land the local continuation primitives separately from cross-session targeting and broad app/docs churn.

options.title: Accept current opt-in boundary
options.body: Maintain the feature as opt-in with documented security and upgrade expectations, accepting the broader review burden in this PR.

recommendation.title: Require exact-head proof and boundary approval
recommendation.body: Resolve the dirty merge state, prove the actual merge result including accepted high-context `request_compaction`, and approve the trusted return-delivery model before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the strongest recurring ownership signal across the agent tools, reply runner, config, and system-event surfaces that need the final boundary call.
